{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZgx7TQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDH17I", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 59, "title": "Implement independent Mode 7 scroll state and its shared register write latch", "body": "## Problem

Mode 7 currently consumes planar BG1 scroll state instead of independent Mode 7 offsets. Writes to `$210D/$210E` update only `scroll` and `scroll_latch`; `$211B–$2120` alone update `m7_latch`. Consequently, interleaved scroll/matrix writes cannot produce the documented Mode 7 register values. See [register writes](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/1bc328f86a3c2e99c79b204f9b18b93f21790153/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L222), [multiplication readback](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/1bc328f86a3c2e99c79b204f9b18b93f21790153/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L290), and [Mode 7 coordinate inputs](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/1bc328f86a3c2e99c79b204f9b18b93f21790153/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L530).

The latest assessment identified scroll/latch reconciliation as a prerequisite to EXTBG. Fix this concrete missing behavior first. No regression was identified in the latest OBJ improvement, and the supplied context lists no open Issues.

## Expected outcome

Implement independent M7HOFS/M7VOFS storage and connect it to the existing Mode 7 register latch, while preserving ordinary BG scrolling.

Specification references are [Anomie's Register Doc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt), `$210D/$210E`, `$211B–$2120`, and multiplication-register descriptions; and [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), the corresponding BG-scroll, Mode 7 offset/matrix, and multiplication descriptions. The repository records reference versions and hashes in its [specification attribution](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/1bc328f86a3c2e99c79b204f9b18b93f21790153/docs/issue-53-validation.md#specification-contract-recorded-before-pixel-expectations). Confirm the relevant passages before freezing test expectations.

The target register semantics are:

- Every `$210D/$210E` write updates both its ordinary BG1 scroll register and its separate Mode 7 offset register. These effects apply independently of the currently selected BGMODE.
- Mode 7 offsets and `$211B–$2120` share one previous-byte latch. Each write commits `(new_byte << 8) | previous_latch` to its addressed Mode 7 register, then replaces that latch with `new_byte`. There is no per-register first/second-write toggle.
- `$210D–$2114` retain the separate planar scroll latch and horizontal fine-bit merge. `$210F–$2114` do not replace the Mode 7 latch; `$211B–$2120` do not replace the planar latch.
- The transform consumes signed 13-bit M7HOFS/M7VOFS values from the new state. Matrix coefficients retain their existing signed 16-bit interpretation.

Scope is register capture and its observable effect on multiplication and static, non-mosaic, non-interlaced Mode 7 BG1 rendering. Keep the implementation local to the PPU and necessary tests/documentation.

EXTBG decoding, priority and composition; transform truncation/clipping corrections; mosaic; interlace; raster/fetch timing; multiplication latency; physical reset retention; and frontend changes are outside scope. BG1 direct-color behavior with EXTBG remains a separate specification question: the scoped assertion in the [Issue #11 record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/1bc328f86a3c2e99c79b204f9b18b93f21790153/docs/issue-11-validation.md) does not resolve it.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: `1bc328f86a3c2e99c79b204f9b18b93f21790153`.

Two focused counterexamples can distinguish the missing behavior:

1. Write `$211C=$00,$01`, then `$210D=$34`, then `$211B=$12`. After ample settling time, `$2134–$2136` should read `$34,$12,$00`: M7A captured `$1234`, and M7B's high byte is `$01`. The baseline source instead computes `$01,$12,$00`. Repeat using `$210E` to establish both offset registers' latch participation.
2. Initialize an identity matrix and zero center, then write `$210D=$15`, `$210F=$42`, `$210D=$00`. M7HOFS should become `$0015`, while ordinary BG1HOFS becomes `$0045`. Switch from a planar mode to Mode 7 and use vertically uniform, nonuniform horizontal graphics to distinguish source columns 21 and 69 without depending on the unresolved vertical row-origin convention.

These are source-derived counterexamples, not observed test results. This planning pass inspected only the repository and supplied context; external specifications were not fetched, tests were not run, and no files changed.

Existing Mode 7 coverage primarily uses ordinary paired writes and identity scenes: [direct-color tests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/1bc328f86a3c2e99c79b204f9b18b93f21790153/crates/snes-core/tests/direct_color.rs) and [pseudo-hires identity control](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/1bc328f86a3c2e99c79b204f9b18b93f21790153/crates/snes-core/tests/ppu_pseudo_hires.rs#L323). Those tests do not establish the missing latch interactions.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the relevant specification passages, versions/hashes, derived register rules, and any disagreement before finalizing oracles. Correct any source-disproved requirement in this draft or existing affected assertions; explain the correction explicitly.
- [ ] Implement separate Mode 7 offset state and the shared latch semantics above. Preserve planar horizontal fine-bit behavior and vertical-scroll behavior.
- [ ] Add original tests covering both offsets, H/V interleaving, cross-register matrix/center writes, immediate single-write capture, planar-only latch interference controls, writes made outside Mode 7, and subsequent mode switching. Verify signed 13-bit consumption with focused identity scenes and ignored upper-bit controls; do not claim general transform-edge accuracy.
- [ ] Add `ppu_mode7_scroll` integration coverage with literal multiplication bytes and independently authored pixel vectors. Include positive/negative offsets, fine/tile boundaries and distinct expected/wrong-source colors. Expected values must not call production register or coordinate helpers.
- [ ] Reproduce behavioral failures against the exact baseline using new tests that compile against its existing APIs. Record failing assertions separately from passing controls; compilation failure is not a counterexample.
- [ ] Add an original MIT source-built CPU guest that initializes graphics and registers through emulated bus writes, performs the latch/readback cases, records results and a sticky completion/pass marker, and displays a distinguishing scroll scene. Bound native execution by instructions and frames. Document source, licensing, build procedure and generated hashes in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`; commit no generated ROM or firmware.
- [ ] Exercise the same guest through the existing browser fixture pattern. Assert completion/results, 256×224 geometry, and literal distinguishing pixels in both actual Wasm framebuffer bytes and canvas readback. Hosts only load, advance and observe; add no public debug API or host state patches.
- [ ] Pass the following checks, using the README's supported toolchain/environment setup:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test ppu_mode7_scroll --test direct_color --test ppu_pseudo_hires --test ppu_offset --test ppu_mode6_offset --test ppu_hires --test ppu_obj_sizes --test ppu_obj_limits
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(cd web && npx playwright install chromium)
npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
```

- [ ] Preserve existing source-built hardware fixtures and cleared Castle/Memory pins, hashes, replay inputs, durations, gameplay/audio assertions and negative controls. Follow the [README validation requirements](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/1bc328f86a3c2e99c79b204f9b18b93f21790153/README.md#validate) and [cleared-game provenance](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/1bc328f86a3c2e99c79b204f9b18b93f21790153/tests/roms/CLEARED-GAMES.md). Require no commercial ROM acquisition.
- [ ] Document actual results, baseline counterexamples, failures/skips and remaining uncertainty. Retain all 24 inventory categories and their complete supplied scopes: 21 partial, `dsp-voices` implemented_unverified, and `ppu-raster`/`pal` unimplemented, with none verified. Preserve the [existing inventory](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/1bc328f86a3c2e99c79b204f9b18b93f21790153/docs/issue-57-validation.md#remaining-uncertainty-and-inventory). Mode 7 remains partial: EXTBG, nonidentity arithmetic/truncation, signed-coordinate/screen-over edges, mosaic, and fetch/raster interactions remain outstanding. Passing these bounded checks establishes neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

Additional original static affine scenes, provided their expectations have independent specification derivations. These do not block completion.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
